mission.title: falco: Falco 0.42.1 random memory usage spikes
mission.description: Falco 0.42.1 random memory usage spikes. This issue affects 6+ users.

steps.title: Identify falco troubleshoot symptoms
steps.description:
Check for the issue in your falco deployment:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n falco -l app.kubernetes.io/name=falco
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=falco -n falco --tail=100 | grep -i error
```
Look for errors or warnings in the logs that may indicate the issue.

steps.title: Review falco configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant falco configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n falco -l app.kubernetes.io/name=falco
kubectl get configmap -n falco -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=falco
```
This issue is reported on Falco 0.42.1 (upgraded from 0.40.0) running the modern eBPF engine with the k8saudit, json and container plugins: pods show random memory spikes and are repeatedly OOM killed. Check whether `falco_libs.thread_table_auto_purging_interval_s` and `thread_table_auto_purging_thread_timeout_s` are set in the Falco ConfigMap — if they are absent, the internal thread table can grow unbounded on busy nodes.

steps.title: Upgrade to Falco 0.43.x and enable thread table auto-purging
steps.description:
Upgrade Falco to 0.43.1 (or later), which includes libs fixes for memory growth, and enable thread table auto-purging so stale thread entries are reclaimed instead of accumulating until the pod is OOM killed:
```bash
helm upgrade falco falcosecurity/falco -n falco \
  --reuse-values \
  --set image.tag=0.43.1
```
Then set the following in `falco.yaml` (via the Helm value `falco.falco_libs` or the Falco ConfigMap):
```yaml
falco_libs:
  snaplen: 80
  thread_table_auto_purging_interval_s: 300
  thread_table_auto_purging_thread_timeout_s: 300
  thread_table_size: 262144
engine:
  kind: modern_ebpf
  modern_ebpf:
    buf_size_preset: 8
    cpus_for_each_buffer: 2
    drop_failed_exit: false
```
Restart the Falco pods to pick up the new configuration:
```bash
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/falco -n falco
```

steps.title: Confirm Falco 0.42.1 random memory usage spikes is resolved
steps.description:
Verify the fix by checking that the original error no longer occurs:
```bash
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=falco -n falco --tail=50 --since=5m
kubectl get events -n falco --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm that the issue symptoms are gone.

resolution.summary: The memory spikes happen because Falco's internal thread table keeps state for every observed process, and on busy nodes stale entries accumulate faster than they are evicted, so resident memory grows until the kubelet OOM-kills the pod. Upgrading to Falco 0.43.1 picks up falcosecurity/libs fixes for this growth, and enabling thread_table_auto_purging_interval_s / thread_table_auto_purging_thread_timeout_s makes Falco periodically purge threads idle longer than the timeout, keeping the table bounded. Capping thread_table_size adds a hard upper bound so a single node cannot grow the table without limit. Source: https://github.com/falcosecurity/falco/issues/3733
codeSnippets:
falco_libs:
  snaplen: 80
  thread_table_auto_purging_interval_s: 300
  thread_table_auto_purging_thread_timeout_s: 300
  thread_table_size: 262144
engine:
  kind: modern_ebpf
  modern_ebpf:
    buf_size_preset: 8
    cpus_for_each_buffer: 2
    drop_failed_exit: false
helm upgrade falco falcosecurity/falco -n falco --reuse-values --set image.tag=0.43.1

prerequisites.description: A running Kubernetes cluster with falco installed or the issue environment reproducible.
